stem.text: A power supply and a solar cell are compared using the potentiometer circuit shown.

stem.alt: Potentiometer circuit diagram: a power supply marked 2.000 V with + and - terminals, a resistor labelled R, a wire PQ with a sliding contact S and length marked 40.0 cm, a solar cell, and a galvanometer.

stem.text: The potentiometer wire PQ is $100.0\,\text{cm}$ long and has a resistance of $5.00\,\Omega$. The power supply has an e.m.f. of $2.000\,\text{V}$ and the solar cell has an e.m.f. of $5.00\,\text{mV}$.
Which resistance $R$ must be used so that the galvanometer reads zero when PS $= 40.0\,\text{cm}$?
